newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LEHMAN PREPARES FOR OPEN WITH FIVE-STROKE WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN PREPARES FOR OPEN WITH FIVE-STROKE WIN.

text.p: Tom Lehman sprinted away from the pack with three successive birdies from the seventh to win the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Saturday in an ideal tune-up for his British Open title defence next week.
The 38-year-old American's fourth round in the 60s, this time a four-under-par 67, gave him victory by five strokes over U.S. Open champion Ernie Els.

Lehman will tackle Royal Troon next week with his confidence high as he attempts to follow his success at Royal Lytham last year and become the first player since Tom Watson in 1983 to retain the British Open title.
He finished with a 19-under-par total of 265 over the exquisite 7,050-yard layout beside the bonny banks of the renowned Scottish lake.
Els closed with a five-under-par 66 to finish 14 under par on 270.
Another South African, Retief Goosen, broke the three-day-old course record by one stroke with a nine-under-par 62 to take third place two shots behind Els on 272.
Paul Curry of England and Joakim Haeggman of Sweden set the record of 63 in Wednesday's opening round.
Pierre Fulke of Sweden, second overnight, dropped to a fourth place tie after a 73 which left him level on 273 with with world number two Greg Norman, who closed with a 68.
